new_findings.section: Evidence precision: per-pull digest coverage vs the committed manifest's own law string (pre-existing since P0; surfaced by this delta audit; NOT introduced by the remediation, which discloses it)
new_findings.evidence: p0/retrieval_manifest.json `law`: 'THIS manifest (sha256 per pull) is committed' and p0/f9_artifact_digests.json `raw_data_note`: 'their content identity is pinned per pull in retrieval_manifest.json (sha256_raw / sha256_gz)'. Bytes: exactly 1 of 111,322 pull records carries sha256_gz/sha256_raw (CKHGF, the single fresh pull of the final pass; n_cached_before_run=111,321); the other 111,321 records are {cached:true, rows:null, status:200} with no digest. The double_pull block pins 5 names only (A/AAON/AAPL/SPY/ZVRA). The preflight verifies pins 'where carried' (honest; disclosed in the remediation handoff known_limitations) and additionally binds plane-wide served counts, the 18-cell census cross-check and the 3 pooled count-series digests - so decision identity IS plane-wide; what is NOT byte-bound for 111,321 names is price/volume content that leaves every GAP/52W-HIGH/VOL-REGIME decision, served count and pooled count unchanged while still shifting scored PnL levels.
new_findings.why: Same evidence-quality class as r1 F-4: a committed identity claim overstates what the artifact carries. A detached R-phase reproducer believing 'sha256 per pull' would expect to re-verify raw bytes per name and cannot. The scored path itself is not opened beyond the residual r1 already accepted (decision-level binding); but at this standard the identity-plane claim must be exact, and the E PASS verdict must make the coverage visible (it does: checks.retrieval_complete.n_digest_pinned_pulls).
new_findings.required_remediation: No scored-path code change required. Before any R-phase reproduction relies on per-pull digests: commit a correction/annotation note (manifest and f9 file are P0 outputs; prefer a correction note over rewriting history) stating that per-pull digests cover fresh-pull records only (1/111,322 on the final plane) and that content identity for cached re-pulls is bound by served-count equality + the census/series comparisons; and archive the E-run data_plane_preflight PASS verdict (which carries n_digest_pinned_pulls) alongside the scored outputs. Owner-informed condition C-8 carries this.

new_findings.section: Remediation handoff doc precision: census-coverage phrasing
new_findings.evidence: ssearch-remediation-f1.handoff.json known_limitations says the census cross-check covers '18/282 cells on the synthetic fixture; proportionally more on the real 47-config grid'. Measured by this audit: on the real grid exactly 6 configs share the 3 arms' states, so the coverage is also 18 cells (the fixture's 18/282 was 6 configs x 3 folds of a 6-config grid, not a proportion). The code and the E verdict artifact are exact (n_cells_checked vs n_configs_total are recorded); only the handoff sentence is wrong.
new_findings.why: Doc imprecision only; no gate consumes the sentence. Recorded so the E verdict's n_cells_checked=18 is not misread as a shortfall against 'proportionally more'.
new_findings.required_remediation: None required for GO; correct the sentence if the handoff is ever superseded/reissued.
